newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Minmet half-yr after-tax loss 32,700 punts.
newsitem.headline: Minmet half-yr after-tax loss 32,700 punts.

text.p: Irish exploration group Minmet Plc said on Thursday that it made an after-tax loss of 32,700 Irish pounds in the six months to June 30, 1996, down from 275,911 in the same period of 1995.
The reduced loss was achieved by dramatically reducing the company's operating overheads, Minmet said in a statement.
It attributed the loss to the administrative, legal and compliance costs of maintaining two publicly-quoted companies, Minmet and its subsidiary Connary Minerals Plc.

The group, which is involved in gold-related activities in Ireland, Portugal, Britain, Russia and Bolivia, said it had made singificant progress in all sectors of its business activities over the last 12 months.
"I look forward to this rapid porgress being maintained into future years," chairman Jeremy Metcalfe said.

Minmet said it had finalised its application with the Securities and Exchange Commission to have its ordinary shares traded in the U.S. and Canada under a sponsored level one American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme. Trading in the ADRs should commence by the end of October 1996, Minmet said.
